body:
I looked into this a bit more today, and have a suspicion of what might be happening.
Using a simpler MRP with a single character, moving in a linear path sideways up a hill ([sideways_uphill.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17844017/sideways_uphill.zip)), I saw that each physics step reports three collisions - one in the direction of motion (more or less), one which represents the recovery from collision with the slope, and then one containing the motion up the hill.  The net movement is the combination of the three.

When moving `4 * (-0.707, 0, -0.707)` at 45 degrees to a 45 degree slope (normal =`(0.707, 0.707, 0)`):

> Collision 0
> Travel (-0.000737, 0, -0.000737) 0.00104166672099
> Remaining (-0.046404, 0, -0.046404) 0.06562500447035
> Collision 1
> Travel (**-0.00037**, 0.000357, **-0.000725**) 0.00088864733698
> Remaining (-0.045679, 0, -0.045679) 0.06459961086512
> Collision 2
> Travel (**-0.037061**, 0.03781, **-0.037423**) 0.0648348480463
> Remaining (0, 0, 0) 0
> 
> Total travel (-0.038167, 0.038167, -0.038884) 0.06652383506298
> Total difference 0.06652353703976 x4 = 3.99141222238541

I noticed that the second collision - the recovery from intersecting the slope - was not in the direction of motion. This makes sense, since the recovery moves you to the closest position outside the collider.  But the effect of this is that the net motion gets deflected slightly downhill from the intended direction, and slowed down (because `collision_normal.dot(velocity) < 0`)! 😬 

So if I'm right, the solution should be to somehow negate the deflection from the recovery collision, but at the moment I don't know how one would go about that.

--

I also noticed that the discrepancy seems to increase with time (or maybe with +y?), which I don't understand since the input velocity is the same every frame! 😖

> Remaining (-0.044194, 0, -0.044194) 0.06249999627471
> Collision 1
> Travel (-0.001077, 0.001424, -0.002503) 0.0030749773141
> Remaining (-0.041691, 0, -0.041691) 0.05895995721221
> Collision 2
> Travel (-0.033334, 0.035858, -0.034592) 0.05994605645537
> Remaining (0, 0, 0) 0
> 
> Total travel (-0.037312, 0.037327, -0.040041) 0.06624817103148
> Total difference: 0.06624826043844 x4 = 3.97489562630653
can confirm this happens on my computer too
